headline: People don't know what they are talking about when they say they say they want the rules to change.
body: Take off your club hats - Man, City, Liverpool, Utd, Brighton, Sunderland etc. Put on your half and half caps- Football and England. Now let's have a discussion. I keep seeing this narrative that the rules are unfair. The red cartel. Man City broke the rules but we don't agree with the rules. Ok. But is that what you really want? If clubs are given cart blanch to do whatever they want what would happen? Well its already been proven. The nation state clubs would win everything. They would ignore any kind of fair play and manipulate the league in any way the fkn wish and fk you if you say otherwise. The only difference is that as well as City, Newcastle would do it as well. Then another club will be bought out by say China ir Russia. Maybe some Princes son decides he wants one for his 18th. You are just replacing one cartel with another. A worse cartel. What's to say they don't decide games will be played in Quatar, Saudi? What's to say they don't jack up prices 500 percent. They don't give a fk about cultural identity. Ok you can say the other owners don't give a fk now. But it will be worse. Much worse. So you say OK let's have an equal transfer spend across clubs. OK. But that's the end of outspending the other leagues. It would reduce the leagues global star power. Also this idea that it would greate 20 equal clubs is nonsense. It will not. Sunderland and Brighton players will still leave for the big clubs. They just will. Why? Because they are bigger clubs. So now players are still leaving to big clubs and to other leagues because the wages etc are on parity and we have a shitter league with poor performances in europe. Is that what you want really? I understand the desire for clubs to want to at least have a chance of winning the league. I really do. But I see no easy solution.
